newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo naphtha little changed despite crude gains.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo naphtha little changed despite crude gains.

text.p: Tokyo naphtha prices were virtually unchanged in lacklustre afternoon trade on Tuesday, ignoring a mild gain on overnight crude markets, traders said.
Near-term naphtha remained under pressure, with the regional supply and demand equation working in favour of buyers, they added.
The one-month spread from first-half August was bid at minus $1.50, while offers were assessed at minus 50 cents.
Offers for second-half August open-spec naphtha were heard at $212.25 per tonne, against bids at $211.25. On Monday, it was traded at $212.00.
Also on Monday, a second-half July contract was sold by a Japanese trading house to a western trader at $210.00.
The seller was rumoured to be offering a first-half July contract at $208.00.
Electric utilities in Japan are about to start building up low sulphur waxy residue and crude oil stocks for summer, when Japan's electricity demand peaks, traders said.

The power firms are expected to build up stocks mainly with cargoes from domestic refiners, and are likely to turn to import cargoes if summer demand exceeds initial expectations, they said. --Tokyo Energy Desk +81-3-3432-8837
